text:
B: Hiya! Oh, there you are. I'm Joanne, I'm in Arnold, just outside Nottingham. How's your day going?
A: Abena. Thornton Heath. It's okay. I'm off today.
B: Oh, lovely, a day off. I thought you looked like you'd just come off shift in your photo. Uniform and that.
A: That photo was after a twelve-hour day. I'm a senior care assistant, care home for older people.
B: Twelve hours, bless you. I do part-time in a primary school office, mornings mostly, so I've got no right to moan, but I do anyway. [laughs] Photocopier jams every Monday, without fail.
A: Hm. Everybody's photocopier jams.
B: [laughs] Universal truth, that. So what are you doing with your day off then?
A: Cooking. Light soup, goat, for the week. And I have a damp problem in my bathroom, my landlord won't fix it. One of the men on this study, the Dutch engineer, told me to hold toilet paper to the fan, see if it pulls. So I'm going to do that.
B: Oh, that's a good tip! I'm going to try that, our fan's been rattling for months. Steve's an electrician and he still hasn't looked at it. Cobbler's children, isn't it.
A: Same everywhere.
B: Can I ask you something, being in care? My mum's got early dementia. I go round three times a week. Some days she's fine, and some days she gets really agitated in the afternoon and accuses me of moving her things. I never know what to do.
A: Afternoons are common. We call it sundowning. Don't argue with her about the things. Even if you know you didn't move them. You say, okay, let's look together. Then you find it, or you make a tea, and she forgets.
B: See, I always argue. I go, Mum, I didn't touch your purse, it's where you left it.
A: You are right, but being right doesn't help her. Also, lights on early, curtains closed before it gets dark. Shadows upset them. And a routine. Same time, same things.
B: That's really helpful, honestly. Nobody's told me any of that. The GP just gives you leaflets.
A: Leaflets. [laughs] Yes. The families who do best are the ones who stop correcting.
B: I'll try that. It does wear you down, you know, I'm practical about it but some days I drive home and just sit in the car for ten minutes.
A: That's normal. You have to look after yourself also. You have help? Brothers, sisters?
B: My sister helps a bit. And Steve's good. The kids are grown up, Leeds and Derby, so they're not round the corner.
A: My son is in Leicester. Near you, no?
B: Oh, not far at all, duck! Forty minutes down the M1. Does he come down to London much?
A: Christmas. He phones on Sundays. That's enough. He has his life.
B: Yeah. I miss mine more than I let on, if I'm honest. House is too quiet.
A: Mm. Quiet is not so bad. You get used to it.
